text: Which set consists of exact solutions to Einstein's field equations that the book presents as containing closed timelike curves (CTCs)?
choices: Godel's rotating universe, the interior of the Kerr metric, and the van Stockum / Tipler rotating cylinder.
The Schwarzschild black hole, the Einstein-Rosen bridge, and flat Minkowski spacetime.
The Casimir effect, the Hafele-Keating atomic-clock experiment, and special-relativistic time dilation.
The Friedmann-Lemaitre expanding universe, de Sitter space, and the Penrose singularity theorem.
explanation: The book lists Godel's 1949 rotating universe, the interior of the Kerr metric for rotating black holes, and the van Stockum (1937) / Tipler (1974) rotating cylinder as GR solutions containing CTCs. The Schwarzschild solution and its non-traversable Einstein-Rosen bridge contain no CTCs, and flat Minkowski spacetime is causally well behaved (choice 1). The Casimir effect, Hafele-Keating, and special-relativistic dilation (choice 2) concern exotic matter and mild forward time travel, not CTC-bearing geometries, and the choice-3 cosmologies do not contain CTCs.
